entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Confederation of African Football (CAF), founded in 1957, is the continental governing body for association football in Africa, organising the Africa Cup of Nations and representing African associations within FIFA. Emerging in the decolonisation era, CAF turned football into a visible arena of pan-African institution-building and soft power.

CAF’s competitions professionalised national teams, redirected player pathways toward European clubs, and became stages for postcolonial politics—boycotts, venue diplomacy, and debates over governance and money. Its relationship with FIFA has oscillated between partnership and contest over World Cup slots and commercial rights.

As African football’s global profile rose in the late twentieth and early twenty-first centuries, CAF stood at the centre of how the continent’s sporting modernity was organised, televised, and contested.
